headline: Industrial gas supply to return to pre-August levels by Tuesday evening
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman says technical issues at an LNG terminal have been resolved, promising a return to normal energy supplies for factories.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman announced that gas supply to industries and factories will return to near previous levels by Tuesday evening. This follows the resolution of a technical problem caused by an accident at one of Bangladesh's two floating LNG terminals.

During a three-hour exchange with business leaders and media professionals in Dhaka, the Prime Minister emphasized that energy and power problems are inherited and cannot be solved quickly. He stated that the government has identified the problems and set timelines for implementation of solutions.

To further secure energy needs, the government is preparing to set up a third floating LNG terminal under a government-to-government arrangement. This new terminal is expected to be connected to the gas supply system by December 2027.

The Prime Minister highlighted that uninterrupted energy and electricity supplies are critical for Bangladesh to achieve its goal of becoming a $1 trillion economy by 2034. He urged business leaders and the media for cooperation to avoid instability that could disrupt the wider economy.
The meeting included high-level officials, including the Commerce Minister, Finance and Planning Adviser, and leaders from FBCCI, BGMEA, and other major business associations.

topic: ducsu displays jinnah photo, students protest
headline_marked: Student [[tears up Jinnah images]] at Ducsu archive in protest
headline: Student tears up Jinnah images at Ducsu archive in protest
summary: A student and activists from the Students' Federation of Bangladesh damaged photographs of Muhammad Ali Jinnah, citing his stance against the Bengali language.
details: A fourth-year Urdu department student, Muhammad Abu Tayab, smashed a frame and tore up photographs of Muhammad Ali Jinnah at the Ducsu archive. He was joined by leaders and activists of the Students' Federation of Bangladesh's Dhaka University unit.

The protest occurred shortly after the renovated archive reopened without a prominent photograph of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, though some newspaper clippings and a wedding photo of his sons remained.
Tayab questioned why a photograph of Jinnah, whom he called a 'villain', should be displayed, stating that the events of 1971 and the Language Movement have not been forgotten.
Following the incident, the Students' Federation placed a photograph in the archive showing convicted war criminal Ghulam Azam being beaten with shoes by the public in 1981.
Ducsu General Secretary SM Farhad defended the display, stating that Jinnah's declaration of Urdu as the sole state language was shown to highlight his opposition to Bangladesh.
The archive had displayed three Jinnah-related images, including a 1948 photo of the Urdu declaration and a 1940 All India Muslim League session photo.
Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal had previously condemned the display of Jinnah's photos and the proposed renaming of Madhur Canteen, calling it a betrayal of the university's liberation spirit.
